cls: Antineoplastic - highly selective MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor
pharm: Selective inhibitor of mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) receptor tyrosine kinase, including MET exon 14 skipping alterations; blocks MET-driven tumor proliferation and survival
quick: 450 mg orally once daily with food
Take with food at about the same time each day
Can cause fetal harm; avoid - use effective contraception
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose
No adjustment in mild-moderate; limited data in severe
No adjustment in mild-moderate; not studied in severe
No specific interaction; limit due to hepatic and GI effects
Edema, pulmonary symptoms (ILD), LFTs, amylase/lipase, pregnancy status
summary: Tepotinib (Tepmetko) is a highly selective oral MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor for adult metastatic NSCLC harboring MET exon 14 skipping alterations. The recommended dose is 450 mg (two 225 mg tablets) orally once daily with food, continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Characteristic toxicity is peripheral edema with hypoalbuminemia, plus interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, hepatotoxicity, and embryo-fetal toxicity. It is a P-gp substrate and weak CYP3A inducer with interactions affecting P-gp substrates and hormonal contraception.
indications: Treatment of adult patients with metastatic NSCLC harboring MET exon 14 skipping alterations

dosage.t: Once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Confirm MET exon 14 skipping with a validated test; dose is two 225 mg tablets
Withhold first for qualifying adverse reactions, then resume at reduced dose if recovered
Permanently discontinue if unable to tolerate 225 mg once daily

admin: Take 450 mg (two 225 mg tablets) by mouth once daily with food at about the same time each day
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush, split, or chew
If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours, then skip it
Select patients based on MET exon 14 skipping alterations using a validated tissue or plasma test
Monitor edema, respiratory status, liver tests, and pancreatic enzymes during treatment
moa: Tepotinib is a potent, ATP-competitive, highly selective inhibitor of the MET receptor tyrosine kinase, including constitutively active variants produced by MET exon 14 skipping alterations that impair receptor degradation. By blocking MET autophosphorylation and downstream signaling through MAPK, PI3K/AKT, and STAT pathways, it inhibits tumor cell proliferation, survival, migration, and angiogenesis in MET-driven NSCLC. Selectivity for MET over other kinases shapes a toxicity profile dominated by edema rather than broad kinase effects.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to tepotinib or any excipient
relative: Prior or active interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis
Concomitant dual strong CYP3A and P-gp inhibitors or strong inducers
monitor: Peripheral and generalized edema with serum albumin
Creatinine (transient rises may not reflect true renal injury)

preg: Based on mechanism and animal findings, tepotinib can cause fetal harm including malformations. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Because tepotinib may reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy, advise an additional nonhormonal method during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on tepotinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild to moderate renal impairment. Tepotinib has not been adequately studied in severe renal impairment; use with caution and monitor closely. Transient creatinine rises on therapy may reflect transporter inhibition rather than kidney injury.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Tepotinib has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment; avoid use if possible or monitor very closely for toxicity.

major: Dual strong CYP3A inhibitors and P-gp inhibitors (e.g., itraconazole) - increase tepotinib exposure; avoid
Strong CYP3A and P-gp inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - decrease exposure; avoid
P-gp substrates with narrow therapeutic index (e.g., digoxin, dabigatran) - tepotinib may increase their exposure; monitor and consider dose reduction of the substrate
moderate: Hormonal contraceptives - tepotinib may reduce efficacy; add a barrier method
Other hepatotoxic or pneumotoxic agents - additive liver or lung injury risk
minor: Acid-reducing agents - no clinically meaningful interaction described; take with food as directed
interactions.food: Take with food; food increases bioavailability and is the labeled condition for the 450 mg dose.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; limit alcohol because of hepatotoxicity and edema risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor ALT, AST, bilirubin, amylase, lipase, albumin, and creatinine; evaluate new pulmonary infiltrates; creatinine rises may be transporter-related.

common: Increased ALT/AST, alkaline phosphatase, amylase, lipase, and creatinine
serious: Pancreatic enzyme elevations with pancreatitis risk
Severe or generalized edema with pleural effusion
rare: QT prolongation reported in clinical experience
emergency: New or worsening dyspnea, cough, or fever (possible pneumonitis) - seek urgent evaluation
Rapid weight gain with marked leg swelling, breathlessness, or chest tightness (severe edema/effusion)
Severe abdominal pain with nausea or vomiting (pancreatitis)
Jaundice, dark urine, or right upper quadrant pain (liver injury)

monitoring: Edema, weight, albumin, and respiratory symptoms at each visit; evaluate promptly for ILD/pneumonitis
Liver function (ALT, AST, bilirubin) at baseline, every 2 weeks for the first 3 months, then monthly
Pregnancy status before starting; contraceptive method (add barrier method)
Renal function, noting transporter-related creatinine rises
counsel: Take two tablets once a day with food at the same time each day; swallow whole
Swelling of the legs, hands, or face is very common: report rapid weight gain, tight shoes, or new breathlessness
Report new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever right away (possible lung inflammation)
Report severe stomach pain, persistent nausea or vomiting, yellowing of skin or eyes, or dark urine
Use effective birth control plus a barrier method during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose; do not breastfeed
Tell your doctor about all medicines including antifungals, seizure drugs, herbal products, and blood thinners
pk: MET inhibition within hours of dosing; tumor responses typically develop over weeks
Median Tmax about 8 hours after a 450 mg dose taken with food
Mean effective elimination half-life about 32 hours
Steady state reached in about 1 to 2 weeks with once-daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted) in original container
pearls: First once-daily oral MET inhibitor for MET exon 14 skipping metastatic NSCLC; confirm alteration by tissue or plasma testing
Must be taken with food; the 450 mg dose (two 225 mg tablets) was studied fed
Peripheral edema is the hallmark toxicity: manage with dose holds, diuretics, albumin checks, and stepwise reduction (450 to 300 to 225 mg)
ILD/pneumonitis can be fatal: withhold for suspected cases and permanently discontinue if confirmed
May render hormonal contraception less effective, so add a barrier method; creatinine rises may be transporter effects, not true renal failure
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered on the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours. If the next dose is due within 8 hours, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once. If vomiting occurs after a dose, take the next dose at the regular time.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for tepotinib overdose. Expected effects reflect exaggerated toxicities including edema, hepatotoxicity, pancreatic enzyme elevation, and pneumonitis. Withhold drug and provide supportive care with monitoring of respiratory status, liver and pancreatic labs, fluid status, and ECG. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
